patient.title: Bevacizumab every 14 days · breast treatment component
patient.context_label: HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer · with paclitaxel
patient.schedule_summary: Bevacizumab infusion on Day 1 of each 14-day cycle with separately prescribed paclitaxel. Continue while the cancer is controlled and treatment is tolerated, with regular review; there is no fixed number of breast-treatment cycles.
patient.purpose: Bevacizumab blocks a signal that helps cancers develop blood vessels. With paclitaxel, it can help delay cancer worsening. The aim in this setting is disease control, with treatment reviewed against benefit and side effects.
patient.indication_text: First-line HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer with paclitaxel. This suite explains the bevacizumab component; paclitaxel and any other treatment need their own plan and assessment.
patient.administration_text: The usual bevacizumab reference dose is 10 mg/kg intravenously every 14 days. The first infusion is over 90 minutes; if tolerated, the second can be over 60 minutes and later infusions over 30 minutes. The team checks the actual prescription, blood pressure, urine and other tests before treatment.
patient.monitoring_summary: Before starting: blood count, kidney and liver tests, urine protein, blood pressure and a heart history/examination. Repeat blood count, kidney/liver tests and urine testing before each cycle; check blood pressure before treatment and after it. Extra checks depend on symptoms and results.
patient.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, oncology pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Bevacizumab
agents.explanation: Binds VEGF, a signal that promotes blood-vessel growth. Blocking VEGF can reduce the blood supply that supports tumour growth; it also affects normal blood vessels and wound healing.
agents.mechanism: Blocks the VEGF blood-vessel growth signal
visual: Less VEGF signalling supports tumour blood vessels
risks: Raised blood pressure and protein in the urine
Bleeding, blood clots and problems with wound healing
Rare bowel perforation, abnormal internal connections called fistulae, or serious wound infection
Rare severe headache, confusion, seizures or vision changes associated with a brain syndrome
Infusion reactions; fatigue and other effects may be increased by the chemotherapy partner
agents.watch: Report bleeding, severe pain, neurological symptoms or wound problems promptly, and attend blood-pressure and urine checks.

anatomy: Severe headache, confusion, seizures or a change in vision need urgent help.
Attend blood-pressure checks; chest pain, breathlessness or a swollen painful leg need urgent help.
Urine checks look for protein. Report new swelling, foamy urine or reduced urine.
Sudden severe abdominal pain needs urgent assessment.
Report bleeding or wounds that are painful, red, spreading or slow to heal.
A new swollen painful leg or sudden breathlessness needs urgent help.
patient.anatomy_note: Symptoms are prompts to contact the team, not a diagnosis. Paclitaxel has additional effects covered in its own guide.

patient.urgent_extra: Seek urgent help for sudden severe abdominal pain, significant bleeding or coughing blood, chest pain, breathlessness, a swollen painful leg, a severe headache, confusion, seizures, a change in vision, or a rapidly painful/red spreading wound. Follow the chemotherapy emergency plan for fever or feeling acutely unwell.

sections.title: Infusion visits
sections.text: The usual bevacizumab reference dose is 10 mg/kg intravenously every 14 days. The first infusion is over 90 minutes; if tolerated, the second can be over 60 minutes and later infusions over 30 minutes. The team checks the actual prescription, blood pressure, urine and other tests before treatment.

sections.title: Checks and samples
sections.text: Allow time for blood tests, a urine sample and blood-pressure checks. A 24-hour urine collection may be needed between visits; confirm when the team needs the result.

sections.title: Partner treatment
sections.text: Paclitaxel may be given on different days from bevacizumab. Bring both treatment plans; a change to one medicine does not automatically change the other.

sections.title: Access and procedures
sections.text: Bevacizumab needs an intravenous cannula or existing suitable central line; the team decides access. Tell the team about surgery, dental work or wounds before booking procedures.

sections.title: Support contacts
sections.text: Keep the daytime and out-of-hours oncology numbers available. If a visit or test is missed, contact the team for a revised plan rather than rearranging treatment yourself.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be chosen
evidence.intro: Adding bevacizumab to paclitaxel can delay worsening of metastatic breast cancer for some people.
evidence.population: First-line HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer with paclitaxel
evidence.interpretation: The supporting study showed a delay in cancer worsening; a longer overall survival was not established. The team weighs this against side effects and treatment burden.
evidence.limitations: The supporting paclitaxel trial used bevacizumab every two weeks. That matches this bevacizumab schedule. Discuss the expected benefit and alternatives for your own situation.

patient.teachback: Which days have bevacizumab and paclitaxel, when are blood-pressure and urine checks, which symptoms need urgent help, and who must know about surgery or a wound?
patient.consent_support: Discuss disease-control goals and alternatives, the lack of established overall-survival improvement in the supporting paclitaxel study, blood-pressure and proteinuria monitoring, bleeding and clotting, bowel perforation/fistula, wound healing, infusion reactions, reproductive precautions and the additional risks of paclitaxel.

support.title: Blood pressure and urine
support.text: Take prescribed blood-pressure medicines as agreed and attend urine checks. If a 24-hour collection is requested, confirm how to collect and return it before the next treatment.

support.title: Surgery, wounds and teeth
support.text: Tell the team about planned operations, dental procedures and any wound that is not healing. Bevacizumab can require a treatment break around procedures; the team sets the timing.

support.title: Separate chemotherapy support
support.text: Bevacizumab itself usually needs no routine anti-sickness premedication. Paclitaxel has separate allergy-prevention, anti-sickness and symptom plans; keep both plans and the emergency contact details.

support.title: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
support.text: Discuss fertility and effective contraception before treatment and continue contraception during treatment and for at least six months after the last bevacizumab dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least six months after the final dose. The partner treatment may require additional precautions.

questions.q: Is this a stand-alone breast treatment?
questions.a: This breast regimen uses bevacizumab with paclitaxel. Any change to the chemotherapy partner or a continuation plan must be agreed with your oncologist.

questions.q: How long will I have treatment?
questions.a: There is no fixed number of breast-treatment cycles. Your team reviews cancer control, side effects and your preferences and agrees when to continue, pause or change.

questions.q: What happens if urine protein or blood pressure rises?
questions.a: The team may repeat tests, treat blood pressure or pause bevacizumab. Severe problems may mean stopping it. Do not restart after a pause without an agreed plan.

questions.q: What if I need an operation or dental work?
questions.a: Tell the oncology team before the procedure. Bevacizumab can slow healing, and the team must coordinate any treatment break and check healing before restarting.

patient.timeline_note: This shows one 14-day bevacizumab cycle without calendar dates. Partner paclitaxel days are separately prescribed. The next cycle is reviewed before it starts.

chronology_notes.title: Different schedules
chronology_notes.text: Bevacizumab repeats every 14 days; the chemotherapy partner can follow a different cycle. Check both plans at every change.

chronology_notes.title: Treatment pauses
chronology_notes.text: A pause for surgery, high blood pressure, proteinuria or another effect needs a new team plan; a calendar alone cannot determine a safe restart.

rationale.summary: Bevacizumab blocks a signal that helps cancers develop blood vessels. With paclitaxel, it can help delay cancer worsening. The aim in this setting is disease control, with treatment reviewed against benefit and side effects.
rationale.setting: First-line HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer with paclitaxel. This suite explains the bevacizumab component; paclitaxel and any other treatment need their own plan and assessment.
rationale.line: First-line metastatic breast treatment with paclitaxel; no adjuvant indication or unrestricted breast monotherapy implied.
factors: Confirm HER2-negative metastatic disease, prior therapy, ECOG, comorbidity, alternatives and patient priorities.
Balance delay in progression against bleeding, hypertension, proteinuria, thrombotic, wound and bowel risks.
Confirm the intended bevacizumab interval, companion schedule and local approval/reimbursement.
alternatives: Other systemic and supportive approaches depend on receptor status, biomarkers, previous therapy, pace of disease and patient preference; no cross-trial ranking is supplied.
limitations: This is a shared bevacizumab component protocol; companion chemotherapy or other SACT is not assessed by these rules.

NCCP 00212 v7 states that no bevacizumab dose adjustment is expected for renal impairment, hepatic impairment or haemodialysis. Review severity, clinical suitability and partner treatment; this does not override proteinuria or other stop/hold rules.

NCCP BP notation >150/100 and >200/110 does not explicitly state how to combine isolated systolic and diastolic abnormalities. A clinician confirms uncontrolled/severe BP; no invented binary calculation is used.
Grade 3 hypertension requires persistence before source discontinuation applies. A new grade 3 event alone is not encoded as a permanent-stop criterion.
NCCP grades in the bevacizumab toxicity table do not identify a CTCAE edition. Existing interface CTCAE v5 descriptions are orientation aids; source grading must be confirmed.
Trial averages do not predict individual benefit. E2100 findings must not be applied to adjuvant disease, other tumour types or every chemotherapy partner.
Normal proteinuria results do not clear unassessed blood pressure, surgical, bleeding or partner-treatment domains.

EMA E2100 Table 10 and the original journal analysis use different assessment/data-cut presentations. This record uses only the EMA Table 10 investigator analysis and its stated overall-survival analysis; no estimates are mixed.

clinical.component_rationale: Bevacizumab binds VEGF and inhibits angiogenesis. Paclitaxel has a distinct cytotoxic mechanism and requires a separate full assessment; a safe bevacizumab domain does not clear paclitaxel.

eligibility_orientation: Adult, ECOG 0–2 and adequate organ function; confirm disease, line, biomarker and partner.
important_cautions: Review prior anthracycline/chest-wall radiotherapy, pelvic radiotherapy, cardiovascular and renal disease, bleeding/clotting history, major/minor procedures and fistula/perforation risk.
Recent pulmonary haemorrhage/haemoptysis >2.5 mL red blood: EMA says do not treat.
Pregnancy is excluded; no breastfeeding during treatment or six months afterwards. Effective contraception during and six months after bevacizumab; reconcile the partner plan.

baseline: Confirm adult first-line HER2-negative metastatic breast disease and paclitaxel plan; review ECOG 0–2 eligibility.
FBC, renal and liver profile; urine protein; blood pressure.
Cardiac history and examination; consider ECHO after prior anthracycline or chest-wall radiotherapy. INR if indicated.
Review surgery/wound healing, bleeding and thromboembolic risks, pelvic radiotherapy and perforation/fistula risks; medicines and reproductive precautions.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal/liver profile, urinalysis, BP and symptom/medicine/wound review.
BP before each cycle and after treatment; partner therapy must also be assessed.
ongoing: BP more frequently if hypertension develops/worsens.
Urine dipstick 2+/3+ or spot urine ≥1 g/L: 24-hour urine collection within 3 days before next dose. Dipstick 4+: hold pending quantification.
24-hour urine >2 to 4 g: hold, recheck every two weeks, resume ≤2 g/24 h after review; >4 g: discontinue.
Warfarin INR weekly until stable then before each cycle.
Consider ECHO at baseline for prior anthracycline/chest-wall radiotherapy; repeat testing is individual, not a copied trastuzumab schedule.
Cancer monitoring follows the individual consultant treatment plan.
access: IV infusion in 100 mL sodium chloride 0.9%; no IV bolus/push.
90-minute first infusion; if tolerated, 60-minute second and then 30-minute later infusions. A rapid/off-label infusion requires separate local policy, consent and governance.

evidence.population: Previously untreated locally recurrent/metastatic breast cancer; trial majority HER2-negative (90%); NCCP breast indication is HER2-negative metastatic disease.
evidence.comparison: Bevacizumab 10 mg/kg every two weeks + weekly paclitaxel versus weekly paclitaxel alone.
evidence.applicability: Direct bevacizumab dose/interval and partner evidence for 00212; trial treatment and current NCCP eligibility still require reconciliation.
evidence.qualitative_result: Improved progression-free survival with the combination; no statistically significant overall-survival improvement established.

endpoints.result_text: Median 11.4 months with bevacizumab/paclitaxel versus 5.8 months with paclitaxel; HR 0.421 (95% CI 0.343–0.516), p<0.0001.
endpoints.interpretation: EMA investigator primary analysis for 10 mg/kg every two weeks plus paclitaxel. Independent-review results are a separate dataset and are not mixed here.
endpoints.analysis_status: Regulatory summary of investigator primary analysis
